fullPassage:
Resilience: Recovering from Difficult Times

Teenage life on social media might seem fun and easy, but being a real teenager presents its own set of challenges, both big and small. So why can some people handle tough times and become stronger while others remain unchanged and helpless? The answer lies in resilience — the ability to adapt to challenging experiences, such as unexpected events or personal difficulties.

The good news is that humans can recover from pressure and hardship and you can develop this skill. However, having resilience does not mean you will never feel stressed or anxious; it is perfectly normal to feel down every now and then. Resilience will not prevent problems, but it will help you face and overcome them.

Think of it like building your body's immune system. Just as you need to be exposed to germs to build immunity, you must experience difficulties to build resilience. In simple terms, resilience is not about being emotionless: Resilience means you experience. You feel. You fail. You hurt. You fall. But you keep going. It is like working out to build your muscles; it takes time and effort to enhance your resilience.

questions.passage: Teenage life on social media might seem fun and easy, but being a real teenager ①<u>present</u> its own set of challenges, both big and small. So why can some people ②<u>handle</u> tough times and become stronger while others remain ③<u>unchanged</u> and helpless? The answer lies in resilience — the ability to ④<u>adapt</u> to challenging experiences, such as unexpected events or personal difficulties.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 주어 'being a real teenager'는 동명사구로 단수 취급하므로, 동사는 presents가 되어야 한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① present → presents: 동명사 주어 = 단수 (3인칭 단수 현재 -s)
✅ ② handle: can + 동사원형
✅ ③ unchanged: remain + 형용사
✅ ④ adapt: the ability to + 동사원형
det.tip: 동명사(V-ing) 주어 = 단수 취급 → 동사에 -(e)s 필요

questions.passage: The good news is that humans can recover from pressure and hardship and you can develop this skill. However, having resilience does not mean you will never feel stressed or anxious; it is perfectly normal ①<u>to feel</u> down every now and then. Resilience will not prevent problems, but it will help you ②<u>face</u> and overcome them. Think of it like ③<u>building</u> your body's immune system. Just as you need ④<u>to expose</u> to germs to build immunity, you must experience difficulties to build resilience.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 원문은 'need to be exposed to germs'로 수동태이다. to expose(능동)가 아닌 to be exposed(수동)가 맞다.
det.analysis:
❌ ④ to expose → to be exposed: 주어(you)가 세균에 노출되는 것이므로 수동태
✅ ① to feel: It is normal to V (가주어 구문)
✅ ② face: help + O + V원형
✅ ③ building: like + 동명사
det.tip: be exposed to(~에 노출되다): 수동태. expose는 '노출시키다'(타동사), 사람이 노출 '되는' 것이므로 수동

questions.passage: Teenage life on social media might seem fun and easy, but being a real teenager presents its own set of challenges. So why can some people handle tough times and become stronger while others remain unchanged? The answer lies in resilience. The good news is that humans can recover from pressure and you can develop this skill. However, having resilience does not mean you will never feel stressed; (A) <u>it is / they are</u> perfectly normal to feel down every now and then. Just as you need to be exposed to germs to build immunity, you must experience difficulties to build resilience. It is like working out to build your muscles; it takes time and effort (B) <u>to enhance / enhancing</u> your resilience.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B)에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) 가주어 it + is + 형용사 + to V 구문이므로 it is. (B) It takes ~ to V 구문이므로 to enhance.
det.analysis:
✅ ① it is — to enhance
(A) it is: 가주어 it (진주어 = to feel down ~)
(B) to enhance: It takes time and effort to V
❌ ② they are: 가주어는 it
❌ ③ enhancing: It takes ~ to V 구문
❌ ④ 둘 다 틀림
det.tip: 가주어 it: It is + 형용사 + to V. It takes + 시간 + to V — 두 구문 모두 가주어 it 사용

So why can some people handle tough times and become ①<u>stronger</u> while others remain ②<u>changed</u> and helpless? questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 원문은 unchanged(변하지 않은)인데 ②에 changed(변한)로 바뀌어 부적절하다. 어떤 사람들은 변하지 않고 무력한 채로 남는다는 문맥.
det.analysis:
❌ ② changed → unchanged: 원문은 'remain unchanged and helpless'
✅ ① stronger: 원문 일치
✅ ③ adapt: 원문 일치
✅ ④ unexpected: 원문 일치
det.tip: unchanged(변하지 않은) ↔ changed(변한). remain + 형용사: ~한 채로 남다

questions.passage: Think of it like building your body's immune system. Just as you need to be ①<u>exposed</u> to germs to build immunity, you must experience difficulties to build resilience. In simple terms, resilience is not about being ②<u>emotionless</u>: Resilience means you experience. You feel. You fail. You hurt. You fall. But you keep going. It is like working out to build your ③<u>muscles</u>; it takes time and effort to ④<u>diminish</u> your resilience.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 원문은 enhance(강화하다)인데 ④에 diminish(줄이다)로 바뀌어 부적절하다.
det.analysis:
❌ ④ diminish → enhance: 원문은 '회복탄력성을 강화하다'
✅ ① exposed: 원문 일치
✅ ② emotionless: 원문 일치
✅ ③ muscles: 원문 일치
det.tip: enhance(강화하다) ↔ diminish(줄이다, 약화시키다)

det.korean: 글은 회복탄력성이 개발 가능한 기술이며, 도전에 대처하는 능력임을 설명한다.

det.korean: 'You feel. You fail. You hurt. You fall.'이라는 부정적 경험 나열 후 'But you keep going'으로 전환 — 어려움 속에서도 멈추지 않는 것이 회복탄력성의 본질.

❌ ② 감정 억제: 'not about being emotionless'
❌ ③ 고통이 무의미: 'You hurt' — 고통도 의미 있는 과정
det.tip: But = 전환 접속사. 앞의 부정적 나열(feel, fail, hurt, fall)과 대비되는 핵심 메시지
